title: Ed Miliband: EU deal not dependent on tuition fees agreement
summary:
Speaking on Friday, Burnham argued that polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said Friday marked a "betrayal of the British people" and a good day for the EU to "try and humiliate" the UK.
Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey said there needed to be more than "tweaks" to the UK's relationship to the EU.
He warned that EU students being allowed to pay domestic university fees would "take £500m, we estimate, out of the higher education sector at a time where there's a lot of pressure on the sector".
He added: "If EU students come and are paying domestic fees, it's not clear we'd be able to increase the number of places for EU students anyway."

title: Andy Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
summary:
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.
The deal, which covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme, is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.
The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.
He believes polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch will use a speech at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) annual conference on Monday to criticise Burnham's EU deal.

title: Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions
summary:
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says reopening the strait is ‘not difficult’ if the US accepts reasonable conditions.
Share Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions on social mediaIran says Qatari mediators have travelled to Tehran as the country’s foreign minister urges the United States to accept Iranian conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Friday night and held two hours of talks with Iranian officials, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said, according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency.
Reopening Hormuz ‘not difficult’The ongoing talks in the region “must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally,” Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday, according to state television.
Iran has restricted shipping through the strait, which normally carried about a fifth of the world’s oil, since the war began.

title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
summary:
A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones at a port in Libya on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
Zelensky added that Ukraine's attack hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship which he claimed was being used to transport weapons.

Peskov declined to comment on the strikes on Russian ships in Libya and said that that information would be provided by Russia's Defence Ministry.

title: Could Iran reverse its stated policy of a civil-only nuclear programme?
summary:

title: Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE
summary:
Behind Somalia’s break with the UAE lies a domestic power struggle with regional leaders close to Abu Dhabi.
Share Why Somalia’s president turned against his former ally, the UAE on social mediaThree years ago, at a town hall meeting in Mogadishu, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud defended one of his country’s most controversial foreign partnerships.
The United Arab Emirates, he declared, was “one of the greatest pillars” of Somalia’s war against the al-Qaeda-linked armed group al-Shabab.
The decision came 10 months after Somalia annulled several commercial, defence and security agreements with the UAE, accusing its former ally of undermining its sovereignty.
Abu Dhabi maintains similar commercial and security ties with Jubbaland, which borders Kenya, although the extent of its involvement there is less publicly documented.
